title: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 06
titleEn: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 06

questions.questionTextEn: The vectors $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = t\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ are orthogonal if $t$ is equal to
questions.explanationEn: Two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero: $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 2t + (-3)(2) + (1)(4) = 2t - 6 + 4 = 2t - 2 = 0 \implies t = 1$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following nitrogenous bases is a **purine**?
questions.explanationEn: **Adenine** and **guanine** are bicyclic **purine** bases (fused pyrimidine and imidazole rings), whereas cytosine, thymine, and uracil are monocyclic **pyrimidine** bases. Hence, option **(D)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For an ideal gas of hard-sphere molecules of fixed diameter $d$, the mean free path ($\lambda$) is proportional to
questions.explanationEn: The mean free path is $\lambda = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2 (N/V)} = \frac{k_B T}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2 P}$, so $\lambda \propto \frac{T}{P}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In **oxy-hemerythrin**, dioxygen binds to the dinuclear non-heme iron active site as
optionsEn: a terminal hydroperoxide ($\text{HO}_2^-$) bound to one $\text{Fe(III)}$ center and hydrogen-bonded to the $\mu$-oxo bridge
a symmetric side-on $\mu\text{-}\eta^2:\eta^2$-peroxo bridge between two $\text{Cu(II)}$ centers
a neutral $\text{O}_2$ molecule bridging two $\text{Fe(II)}$ centers without oxidation
questions.explanationEn: In deoxy-hemerythrin, two $\text{Fe(II)}$ centers are linked by a $\mu$-hydroxo and two $\mu$-carboxylato bridges. Upon $\text{O}_2$ binding, two-electron oxidation of the di-iron core and proton transfer from the $\mu\text{-OH}$ bridge produce a $\mu$-oxo-bridged di-$\text{Fe(III)}$ site with a terminal hydroperoxide ($\text{Fe}^{3+}-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{H}$) hydrogen-bonded to the $\mu$-oxo oxygen.

questions.questionTextEn: In singlet methylene ($:\text{CH}_2$), the hybridization of the carbon atom and the location of its two non-bonding electrons, respectively, are
optionsEn: $sp^2$ and paired in the $sp^2$ hybrid orbital
$sp^2$ and unpaired in one $sp^2$ and one $2p$ orbital
$sp$ and paired in an unhybridized $2p$ orbital
questions.explanationEn: In singlet methylene ($:\text{CH}_2$), the carbon atom is $sp^2$-hybridized with a bent geometry ($\angle\text{H}-\text{C}-\text{H} \approx 102^\circ$). Its two non-bonding electrons are spin-paired in the lower-energy $sp^2$ hybrid orbital, leaving the unhybridized $2p$ orbital vacant. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Citral (geranial/neral, $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{16}\text{O}$), the major component of lemongrass oil, is an acyclic monoterpene containing which functional group?
questions.explanationEn: Citral (3,7-dimethylocta-2,6-dienal) is a mixture of $(E)$-geranial and $(Z)$-neral, both of which are acyclic monoterpene **$\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated aldehydes**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following compounds produces an intense violet or reddish-violet coloration with neutral aqueous $\text{FeCl}_3$ solution?
questions.explanationEn: Neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ forms colored iron(III)–enolate/phenolate complexes with phenols and enolizable $\beta$-dicarbonyl compounds such as ethyl acetoacetate (which contains significant enol content).

questions.questionTextEn: At any fixed temperature, the ratio of the root-mean-square speed ($v_{\text{rms}}$) to the most probable speed ($v_{\text{mp}}$) of an ideal gas is
questions.explanationEn: Since $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$ and $v_{\text{mp}} = \sqrt{\frac{2RT}{M}}$, their ratio is $\frac{v_{\text{rms}}}{v_{\text{mp}}} = \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} = \sqrt{3} : \sqrt{2}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a chemical reaction whose overall order is $3/2$, the SI-derived unit of the rate constant $k$ (with concentration in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ and time in $\text{s}$) is
questions.explanationEn: For an $n$-th order reaction, the rate constant $k$ has units $(\text{concentration})^{1-n}\text{ time}^{-1}$. Substituting $n = 3/2$ gives $1 - n = -1/2$, so the units are $(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^{-1/2}\text{ s}^{-1} = \text{mol}^{-1/2}\text{ dm}^{3/2}\text{ s}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In diborane ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$), the number of terminal $\text{B}-\text{H}$ bonds and three-center two-electron ($3\text{c}\text{--}2\text{e}$) $\text{B}-\text{H}-\text{B}$ bridging bonds, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: Diborane ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$, $D_{2h}$) consists of four coplanar terminal $2\text{c}\text{--}2\text{e}$ $\text{B}-\text{H}$ bonds ($119\text{ pm}$) and two bridging $3\text{c}\text{--}2\text{e}$ $\text{B}-\text{H}-\text{B}$ banana bonds ($131\text{ pm}$) lying perpendicular to the terminal plane.

questions.questionTextEn: The bifluoride anion $[\text{F}-\text{H}-\text{F}]^-$ in $\text{KHF}_2$ is notable because it features
optionsEn: a bent geometry with two unequal $\text{H}-\text{F}$ distances
a linear, centrosymmetric ($D_{\infty h}$) very strong $3\text{c}\text{--}4\text{e}$ hydrogen bond with equal $\text{F}-\text{H}$ distances
a purely ionic interaction between $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{F}_2^{2-}$
an unstable hydrogen bond weaker than that in ice
questions.explanationEn: In $[\text{F}-\text{H}-\text{F}]^-$, the proton lies exactly midway between the two fluorine atoms in a linear $D_{\infty h}$ geometry ($d_{\text{H}-\text{F}} \approx 114\text{ pm}$), forming one of the strongest known hydrogen bonds ($\sim 160\text{--}230\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), well described by $3\text{c}\text{--}4\text{e}$ MO bonding.

questions.questionTextEn: The thermal Diels–Alder reaction of 1-methoxybuta-1,3-diene with acrolein ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}$) gives predominantly which regioisomer?
optionsEn: an equal $1:1$ mixture of 'ortho' and 'meta' adducts
questions.explanationEn: By the **ortho/para rule** (and FMO coefficient matching) for normal-electron-demand Diels–Alder reactions, a 1-substituted electron-rich diene (1-methoxybuta-1,3-diene, largest HOMO coefficient at C4) pairs its C4 carbon with the unsubstituted $\beta$-carbon of the electron-deficient dienophile (acrolein, largest LUMO coefficient at $\text{C}_\beta$). Consequently, the $-\text{OMe}$ (at C1) and $-\text{CHO}$ (at $\text{C}_\alpha$) end up **1,2 ('ortho')** to each other, forming **2-methoxycyclohex-3-ene-1-carbaldehyde**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Beckmann rearrangement of $(E)$-acetophenone oxime (where $-\text{OH}$ is *anti* to $-\text{Ph}$ and *syn* to $-\text{CH}_3$) upon treatment with $\text{PCl}_5$ followed by aqueous workup yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: The **Beckmann rearrangement** is strictly stereospecific: the group located ***anti* ($180^\circ$)** to the oxime leaving group migrates to nitrogen. In $(E)$-acetophenone oxime, the **phenyl group** is *anti* to $-\text{OH}$, so phenyl migrates to nitrogen to form the nitrilium ion, which hydrolyzes and tautomerizes to **$N$-phenylacetamide (acetanilide)**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Nitration of pyridine $N$-oxide with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $100\,^\circ\text{C}$ yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: Unlike pyridine (which is strongly deactivated and nitrates sluggishly at C3), **pyridine $N$-oxide** has an oxygen lone pair that donates electron density by resonance ($+M$) into **C2 and C4**. Because C2 is more sterically hindered and subject to stronger $-I$ withdrawal by $\text{N}^+$, nitration occurs predominantly at **C4**, yielding **4-nitropyridine $N$-oxide** (which can be deoxygenated to 4-nitropyridine with $\text{PCl}_3$). Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: When the UV–Vis spectrum of mesityl oxide (4-methylpent-3-en-2-one, an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone) is recorded in ethanol instead of hexane, the $\pi \to \pi^*$ and $n \to \pi^*$ absorption bands shift, respectively, toward
optionsEn: longer wavelength (bathochromic) for $\pi \to \pi^*$ and shorter wavelength (hypsochromic) for $n \to \pi^*$
shorter wavelength (hypsochromic) for $\pi \to \pi^*$ and longer wavelength (bathochromic) for $n \to \pi^*$
questions.explanationEn: In polar protic ethanol, hydrogen bonding stabilizes the ground-state oxygen lone pair ($n$) strongly, increasing the $n \to \pi^*$ energy gap (hypsochromic/blue shift). Conversely, the more polar $\pi^*$ excited state is stabilized more than the $\pi$ ground state, decreasing the $\pi \to \pi^*$ gap (bathochromic/red shift).

questions.questionTextEn: In an iodometric titration of liberated $\text{I}_2$ with standard $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$, starch indicator is added **just before the endpoint** (when the brown solution turns pale straw-yellow) rather than at the start of the titration because
optionsEn: starch reacts directly with $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$ at high $\text{I}_2$ concentration
high concentrations of $\text{I}_2$ form a slowly dissociating (or partially irreversible) starch–iodine complex, causing a sluggish, smeared endpoint
starch is insoluble in aqueous $\text{KI}$ solutions
starch catalyzes the air oxidation of $\text{I}^-$ to $\text{I}_2$
questions.explanationEn: At high $\text{I}_2$ concentrations, iodine becomes tightly trapped inside the helical amylose chains of starch and releases slowly during titration, leading to a diffuse endpoint and over-titration. Adding starch near the endpoint ensures a sharp blue-to-colorless transition.

questions.questionTextEn: In the catalytic hydrogenation of an unhindered terminal alkene using Wilkinson's catalyst, $[\text{RhCl(PPh}_3)_3]$, the correct chronological sequence of elementary organometallic steps is
optionsEn: Phosphine dissociation $\to$ Oxidative addition of $\text{H}_2$ $\to$ Alkene coordination $\to$ Migratory insertion $\to$ Reductive elimination of alkane
Reductive elimination $\to$ Alkene coordination $\to$ Oxidative addition of $\text{H}_2$ $\to$ Migratory insertion
Migratory insertion $\to$ Phosphine dissociation $\to$ Oxidative addition of $\text{H}_2$ $\to$ Reductive elimination
Alkene coordination $\to$ Reductive elimination $\to$ Oxidative addition of $\text{H}_2$ $\to$ Phosphine dissociation
questions.explanationEn: In the Halpern mechanism for Wilkinson's catalyst: (1) dissociation of one $\text{PPh}_3$ gives the $14\text{ e}^-$ active species $[\text{RhCl(PPh}_3)_2]$; (2) oxidative addition of $\text{H}_2$ gives $16\text{ e}^-$ $[\text{Rh(H)}_2\text{Cl(PPh}_3)_2]$; (3) $\eta^2$-alkene coordination forms an $18\text{ e}^-$ intermediate; (4) $1,2$-migratory insertion forms a $16\text{ e}^-$ alkyl-hydrido complex; (5) reductive elimination releases the alkane and regenerates $[\text{RhCl(PPh}_3)_2]$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a Hittorf electrolysis of aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$ using **silver electrodes**, passage of $0.010\text{ F}$ of charge causes the anode compartment to **gain** $0.0053\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Ag}^+$. The transport number of $\text{Ag}^+$ ($t_+$) is
questions.explanationEn: With attackable $\text{Ag}$ electrodes, $0.010\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Ag}^+$ dissolves from the anode while $t_+ (0.010)\text{ mol}$ migrates out of the anode compartment toward the cathode. Thus net gain at the anode $= 0.010(1 - t_+) = 0.0053 \implies 1 - t_+ = 0.53 \implies t_+ = 0.47$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Match the following carbonyl compounds with their characteristic IR $\text{C=O}$ stretching frequencies:
- **P**: $\beta$-propiolactone (4-membered cyclic ester)
- **Q**: $\gamma$-butyrolactone (5-membered cyclic ester)
- **R**: $\delta$-valerolactone (6-membered cyclic ester)
- **S**: cyclohex-2-en-1-one (conjugated cyclic ketone)
questions.explanationEn: Ring strain raises $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ progressively as lactone ring size decreases: $\beta$-lactone ($\sim 1820\text{ cm}^{-1}$) $>$ $\gamma$-lactone ($\sim 1770\text{ cm}^{-1}$) $>$ strain-free $\delta$-lactone ($\sim 1735\text{ cm}^{-1}$, like acyclic esters). Conjugation in cyclohex-2-en-1-one lowers $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ to $\sim 1680\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Friedel–Crafts acetylation of naphthalene with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}/\text{AlCl}_3$ in $\text{CS}_2$ gives predominantly 1-acetylnaphthalene, whereas performing the same reaction in **nitrobenzene** solvent gives predominantly
optionsEn: 2-acetylnaphthalene due to the bulkier solvated $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}\cdot\text{AlCl}_3\cdot\text{PhNO}_2$ electrophile
questions.explanationEn: In polar nitrobenzene, $\text{PhNO}_2$ coordinates strongly to the $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}\cdot\text{AlCl}_3$ complex, creating a sterically bulky acylating agent. Steric hindrance with the peri-hydrogen at C8 disfavors C1 attack, directing acetylation predominantly to the less hindered **C2 position** to yield **2-acetylnaphthalene**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Using Slater's rules, the effective nuclear charges ($Z_{\text{eff}}$) experienced by a $3d$ electron and a $4s$ electron in a neutral iron atom ($\text{Fe}$, $Z = 26$, configuration $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^6 4s^2$), respectively, are
questions.explanationEn:
Grouping the orbitals of $\text{Fe}$ ($Z=26$) as $(1s)^2(2s,2p)^8(3s,3p)^8(3d)^6(4s)^2$:
- For a $3d$ electron: $4s$ electrons do not shield ($0$); five other $3d$ electrons contribute $5 \times 0.35 = 1.75$; the $18$ inner electrons contribute $18 \times 1.00 = 18.00$. Thus $\sigma_{3d} = 19.75$ and $Z_{\text{eff}}(3d) = 26 - 19.75 = 6.25$.
- For a $4s$ electron: one other $4s$ electron contributes $0.35$; the $14$ electrons in $n=3$ ($3s^2 3p^6 3d^6$) contribute $14 \times 0.85 = 11.90$; the $10$ electrons in $n \le 2$ contribute $10 \times 1.00 = 10.00$. Thus $\sigma_{4s} = 22.25$ and $Z_{\text{eff}}(4s) = 26 - 22.25 = 3.75$.

questions.questionTextEn: The termolecular gas-phase oxidation $2\text{NO} + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{NO}_2$ follows a pre-equilibrium mechanism: $2\text{NO} \xrightleftharpoons[k_{-1}]{k_1} \text{N}_2\text{O}_2$ (fast, $\Delta H^\circ = -40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), followed by $\text{N}_2\text{O}_2 + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{k_2} 2\text{NO}_2$ (slow, $E_{a2} = +25\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). The overall apparent activation energy $E_{a,\text{app}}$ is
questions.explanationEn: The effective rate constant is $k_{\text{eff}} = K_{\text{eq}} k_2 = \frac{k_1}{k_{-1}} k_2$. Since $K_{\text{eq}} \propto e^{-\Delta H^\circ/RT}$ and $k_2 \propto e^{-E_{a2}/RT}$, the apparent activation energy is $E_{a,\text{app}} = \Delta H^\circ + E_{a2} = -40 + 25 = -15\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Determine the absolute configuration at C2 and C3 of the following Fischer projection of 2-bromo-3-chlorobutane:
- Top (C1): $-\text{CH}_3$
- C2: $-\text{Br}$ on the right, $-\text{H}$ on the left
- C3: $-\text{H}$ on the right, $-\text{Cl}$ on the left
- Bottom (C4): $-\text{CH}_3$
questions.explanationEn: At **C2**: priorities are (1) $-\text{Br}$ (right), (2) $-\text{CH(Cl)CH}_3$ (bottom), (3) $-\text{CH}_3$ (top), (4) $-\text{H}$ (left, horizontal). The path $1 \to 2 \to 3$ goes clockwise ($R$ apparent); reversing because $-\text{H}$ is horizontal gives **$2S$**. At **C3**: priorities are (1) $-\text{Cl}$ (left), (2) $-\text{CH(Br)CH}_3$ (top), (3) $-\text{CH}_3$ (bottom), (4) $-\text{H}$ (right, horizontal). The path $1 \to 2 \to 3$ goes clockwise ($R$ apparent); reversing because $-\text{H}$ is horizontal gives **$3S$**. Thus the configuration is **$(2S, 3S)$**.

questions.questionTextEn:
Using the free-electron 1D particle-in-a-box model for 1,3,5-hexatriene ($6\,\pi$ electrons confined to a box of length $L = 9.8\text{ \AA}$), the wavelength of the lowest-energy $\pi \to \pi^*$ electronic transition (HOMO $\to$ LUMO) is closest to
[Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$, $m_e = 9.109 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$, $c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: Six $\pi$-electrons fill $n = 1, 2, 3$ (two per level), so HOMO is $n = 3$ and LUMO is $n = 4$. Thus $\Delta E = (4^2 - 3^2)\frac{h^2}{8m_e L^2} = \frac{7h^2}{8m_e L^2}$. The wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{hc}{\Delta E} = \frac{8m_e c L^2}{7h} = \frac{8(9.109\times 10^{-31})(3.0\times 10^8)(9.8\times 10^{-10})^2}{7(6.626\times 10^{-34})} = 4.53 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 453\text{ nm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For any single-phase homogeneous substance with molar volume $V_m$, isobaric thermal expansion coefficient $\alpha$, and isothermal compressibility $\kappa_T$, the difference $C_{P,m} - C_{V,m}$ is equal to
questions.explanationEn: From the general thermodynamic identity $C_{P,m} - C_{V,m} = T\left(\frac{\partial V_m}{\partial T}\right)_P\left(\frac{\partial P}{\partial T}\right)_{V_m}$ and substituting $\alpha = \frac{1}{V_m}\left(\frac{\partial V_m}{\partial T}\right)_P$ and $\kappa_T = -\frac{1}{V_m}\left(\frac{\partial V_m}{\partial P}\right)_T$, we obtain $C_{P,m} - C_{V,m} = \frac{TV_m\alpha^2}{\kappa_T}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which reagent sequence converts **aniline** cleanly into **1,3,5-tribromobenzene**?
questions.explanationEn:
1. Excess $\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$ brominates strongly activated aniline at all three *ortho*/*para* positions to yield **2,4,6-tribromoaniline**.
2. Diazotization with $\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}$ at $0\,^\circ\text{C}$ gives 2,4,6-tribromobenzenediazonium chloride.
3. Reductive deamination with hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) replaces $-\text{N}_2^+$ with $-\text{H}$, yielding **1,3,5-tribromobenzene**. (Option D would yield 1,2,3,5-tetrabromobenzene.) Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The oxygen-binding curve of myoglobin ($\text{Mb}$) is hyperbolic whereas that of hemoglobin ($\text{Hb}$) is sigmoidal. Their respective Hill coefficients ($n_H$) are approximately
questions.explanationEn: Monomeric myoglobin has a single heme binding site and shows non-cooperative binding ($n_H = 1.0$, hyperbolic). Tetrameric hemoglobin exhibits positive cooperativity across its four subunits with an experimental Hill coefficient of $n_H \approx 2.8$ (sigmoidal).

questions.questionTextEn: The Henry's law constant for a gas dissolved in water at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$ is $K_H = 4.0 \times 10^4\text{ bar}$ (defined by $P = K_H x$). The equilibrium mole fraction of this gas in water under a partial pressure of $2.0\text{ bar}$ is
questions.explanationEn: By Henry's law, $x = \frac{P}{K_H} = \frac{2.0\text{ bar}}{4.0 \times 10^4\text{ bar}} = 5.0 \times 10^{-5}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For the Pauli matrices $\sigma_x = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\sigma_z = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$, the commutator $[\sigma_x, \sigma_z] = \sigma_x\sigma_z - \sigma_z\sigma_x$ is equal to
questions.explanationEn: Computing the products directly: $\sigma_x\sigma_z = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\sigma_z\sigma_x = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. Subtracting gives $[\sigma_x, \sigma_z] = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a pure ideal gas at pressure $P$ and absolute temperature $T$, the total number of bimolecular collisions per unit volume per unit time ($Z_{11}$) is proportional to
questions.explanationEn: The bimolecular collision density is $Z_{11} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\pi d^2 \bar{v} \left(\frac{N}{V}\right)^2$. Since $\bar{v} \propto T^{1/2}$ and $\frac{N}{V} = \frac{P}{k_B T} \propto \frac{P}{T}$, we get $Z_{11} \propto T^{1/2}\left(\frac{P}{T}\right)^2 = \frac{P^2}{T^{3/2}}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about binary liquid solutions is/are correct?
optionsEn: For an ideal binary solution, the chemical potential of component $i$ is $\mu_i = \mu_i^* + RT\ln x_i$.
A chloroform–acetone mixture shows negative deviation from Raoult's law due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding between unlike molecules.
An azeotropic mixture boils at a constant temperature without change in composition.
For a solution obeying Raoult's law, the vapor phase is always richer in the less volatile component.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A), (B), (C) True:** Standard ideal chemical potential, $\text{CHCl}_3\text{--}(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CO}$ H-bonding gives negative deviation, and azeotropes distill at constant composition ($y_i = x_i$).
- **(D) False:** By Konowaloff's rule, the vapor phase is always richer in the *more* volatile component.

questions.questionTextEn: In a photoelectric effect experiment conducted above the threshold frequency ($\nu > \nu_0$), the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: Increasing the intensity of incident light at fixed frequency increases the photoelectric current.
Increasing the intensity of incident light at fixed frequency increases the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons.
The slope of the plot of stopping potential $V_s$ versus incident frequency $\nu$ is $h/e$, independent of the metal.
Emission of photoelectrons occurs virtually instantaneously upon illumination.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** Higher intensity means more photons per second, ejecting more photoelectrons per second (higher current).
- **(B) False:** $K_{\max} = h\nu - \phi$ depends only on frequency $\nu$ and work function $\phi$, not intensity.
- **(C) True:** $V_s = (h/e)\nu - \phi/e$ has universal slope $h/e$.
- **(D) True:** Photon absorption is a single-quantum event with negligible time lag.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about silicones (polysiloxanes) is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: They contain a repeating $(-\text{R}_2\text{Si}-\text{O}-)_n$ backbone with strong $\text{Si}-\text{O}$ bonds.
They are water-repellent (hydrophobic) due to the nonpolar alkyl/aryl groups surrounding the siloxane chain.
They possess high thermal stability and good electrical insulating properties.
Hydrolysis of $\text{R}_3\text{SiCl}$ alone produces a long-chain linear silicone polymer.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all classic properties of silicones.
- (D) False: Hydrolysis of $\text{R}_3\text{SiCl}$ yields $\text{R}_3\text{SiOH}$, which condenses only to the dimer hexaalkyldisiloxane ($\text{R}_3\text{Si}-\text{O}-\text{SiR}_3$), not a long-chain polymer.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about **quinoline** and **isoquinoline** is/are correct?
optionsEn: Both quinoline and isoquinoline are $10\,\pi$-electron bicyclic heteroaromatic compounds.
Electrophilic nitration of quinoline with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ occurs predominantly on the benzene ring at C5 and C8.
Nucleophilic substitution (Chichibabin reaction with $\text{NaNH}_2$) on quinoline occurs preferentially at C2.
Electrophilic nitration of quinoline occurs predominantly on the pyridine ring at C2.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Both are benzopyridines with $10\,\pi$ electrons ($4n+2$, $n=2$).
- **(B) Correct (and D Incorrect):** The pyridine ring is strongly deactivated (especially when protonated in $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$), so nitration occurs on the benzene ring at **C5 and C8**.
- **(C) Correct:** Nucleophiles attack the electron-deficient pyridine ring of quinoline preferentially at **C2**.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following compounds will undergo a Cannizzaro reaction upon heating with concentrated aqueous $\text{NaOH}$?
questions.explanationEn:
The Cannizzaro reaction (base-induced disproportionation to alcohol + carboxylate) occurs with aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens:
- **(A) Pivalaldehyde ($t\text{-BuCHO}$):** No $\alpha$-H $\implies$ undergoes Cannizzaro.
- **(B) 4-Chlorobenzaldehyde:** No $\alpha$-H $\implies$ undergoes Cannizzaro.
- **(C) Formaldehyde:** No $\alpha$-H $\implies$ undergoes Cannizzaro.
- **(D) Isobutyraldehyde ($\text{Me}_2\text{CHCHO}$):** Has an $\alpha$-H $\implies$ undergoes aldol addition instead.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) comparing hemocyanin ($\text{Hc}$) and hemerythrin ($\text{Hr}$) is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: Neither hemocyanin nor hemerythrin contains a porphyrin (heme) ring.
Both oxy-hemocyanin and oxy-hemerythrin are diamagnetic due to strong antiferromagnetic coupling between their two oxidized metal centers.

The $\text{O}-\text{O}$ stretching frequency in resonance Raman spectroscopy shows that $\text{O}_2$ is reduced to the peroxide ($\text{O}_2^{2-}$ / $\text{HO}_2^-$) level in both oxy-Hc ($\sim 750\text{ cm}^{-1}$) and oxy-Hr ($\sim 844\text{ cm}^{-1}$).
Both proteins bind one $\text{O}_2$ molecule per metal ion ($1:1$ $\text{M}:\text{O}_2$ stoichiometry).
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all true.
- (D) False: Both are dinuclear oxygen carriers that bind one $\text{O}_2$ molecule per **two** metal ions ($2\text{ Cu}:1\text{ O}_2$ in $\text{Hc}$ and $2\text{ Fe}:1\text{ O}_2$ in $\text{Hr}$).

questions.questionTextEn: Comparing the Langmuir and Freundlich adsorption isotherms, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: The Freundlich isotherm is empirical and fails to predict saturation coverage at very high pressures.
In the Freundlich isotherm $x/m = k P^{1/n}$, $1/n$ typically lies between $0$ and $1$.
The Langmuir isotherm reduces to $x/m \propto P$ at very low pressures and $x/m = \text{constant}$ at very high pressures.
The Langmuir isotherm assumes that the enthalpy of adsorption decreases logarithmically with surface coverage $\theta$.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are true. (D) describes the **Freundlich** (or Temkin, linearly) assumption of surface heterogeneity; the Langmuir model assumes a **constant** enthalpy of adsorption independent of $\theta$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following oxoacids of sulfur contain(s) at least one direct $\text{S}-\text{S}$ bond?
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$: $\text{HO}-\text{SO}(=\text{S})-\text{OH}$ has an $\text{S}=\text{S}$ bond. True.
- (B) $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_6$: $\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{SO}_2-\text{OH}$ has an $\text{S}-\text{S}$ bond. True.
- (C) $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$: has an $\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{S}$ peroxo bridge, NO $\text{S}-\text{S}$ bond. False.
- (D) $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_4$: $\text{HO}-\text{SO}-\text{SO}-\text{OH}$ has an $\text{S}-\text{S}$ bond. True.

questions.questionTextEn: For a reversible galvanic cell at constant pressure and temperature, the correct thermodynamic relation(s) is/are
questions.explanationEn: All four relations follow directly from $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ$: $\Delta S^\circ = -(\partial \Delta G^\circ/\partial T)_P = nF(\partial E^\circ/\partial T)_P$; $\Delta H^\circ = \Delta G^\circ + T\Delta S^\circ = -nF[E^\circ - T(\partial E^\circ/\partial T)_P]$; and $\Delta C_P^\circ = T(\partial \Delta S^\circ/\partial T)_P = nFT(\partial^2 E^\circ/\partial T^2)_P$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following acidity comparison(s) in aqueous solution is/are correct?
optionsEn: Formic acid ($\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$) is more acidic than acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$).
2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid) is acidic enough to liberate $\text{CO}_2$ from aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$.
Cyclopentadiene ($\text{p}K_a \approx 16$) is more acidic than terminal alkynes ($\text{p}K_a \approx 25$).
Phenol is more acidic than benzoic acid.
questions.explanationEn: (A) Formic acid ($\text{p}K_a = 3.75$) $>$ acetic acid ($4.76$) due to $+I$ of $\text{CH}_3$. (B) Picric acid ($\text{p}K_a \approx 0.4$) is much stronger than $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$ ($6.35$) and evolves $\text{CO}_2$ from $\text{NaHCO}_3$. (C) Aromaticity of $\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^-$ gives $\text{p}K_a \approx 16 < 25$. (D) False: benzoic acid ($4.20$) is much stronger than phenol ($9.95$).

questions.questionTextEn: A chiral catalyst produces a product with $72\%$ enantiomeric excess ($\text{ee}$). The percentage of the **major** enantiomer in the product mixture is _______ $\%$. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: If $x$ is the percentage of the major enantiomer, then $x - (100 - x) = 72 \implies 2x = 172 \implies x = 86\%$.

questions.questionTextEn: If $f(x) = \ln(x^2 + 3x + 1)$, the value of $f'(1)$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: By the chain rule, $f'(x) = \frac{2x + 3}{x^2 + 3x + 1}$. Evaluating at $x = 1$ gives $f'(1) = \frac{2(1) + 3}{1 + 3 + 1} = \frac{5}{5} = 1$.

questions.questionTextEn: The minimum number of moles of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ required to convert $1\text{ mol}$ of 4-hydroxybutan-2-one ($\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$) completely into 3-methylbutane-1,3-diol (after aqueous workup) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The first mole of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ is consumed in acid–base deprotonation of the protic $-\text{OH}$ group (releasing $\text{CH}_4$), and the second mole undergoes nucleophilic 1,2-addition to the ketone carbonyl. Hence, a minimum of **$2$** moles of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ is required.

questions.questionTextEn: A steady current of $2.0\text{ A}$ is passed through aqueous $\text{CuSO}_4$ for $965\text{ s}$. Taking $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$ and atomic mass of $\text{Cu} = 63.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, the mass of copper deposited at the cathode is _______ $\text{g}$. *(round off to three decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: Moles of electrons $= \frac{It}{F} = \frac{2.0 \times 965}{96500} = 0.020\text{ mol}$. Since $n = 2$ for $\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^- \to \text{Cu}$, moles of $\text{Cu} = 0.010\text{ mol}$, so mass $= 0.010 \times 63.5 = 0.635\text{ g}$.

questions.questionTextEn: If the solubility product of $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$ in pure water is $K_{sp} = 3.2 \times 10^{-11}$, its molar solubility is $X \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1}$. The value of $X$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: For $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4(s) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{Ag}^+ + \text{CrO}_4^{2-}$, $K_{sp} = (2s)^2(s) = 4s^3$. Thus $s^3 = \frac{3.2 \times 10^{-11}}{4} = 8.0 \times 10^{-12} \implies s = 2.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1}$, giving $X = 2$.

questions.questionTextEn: A liquid boils at $400\text{ K}$ under $1\text{ atm}$ pressure with a molar enthalpy of vaporization $\Delta H_{\text{vap}} = 35.2\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Its molar entropy of vaporization $\Delta S_{\text{vap}}$ is _______ $\text{J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: At the normal boiling point, phase transition occurs reversibly at constant $T$ and $P$: $\Delta S_{\text{vap}} = \frac{\Delta H_{\text{vap}}}{T_b} = \frac{35{,}200\text{ J mol}^{-1}}{400\text{ K}} = 88\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a complexometric titration at $\text{pH } 10$, the volume of $0.025\text{ M}$ $\text{Na}_2\text{H}_2\text{EDTA}$ required to completely titrate $25.0\text{ mL}$ of $0.040\text{ M}$ $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ solution is _______ $\text{mL}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn:
Since $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ reacts with EDTA in a $1:1$ molar ratio:
$M_{\text{EDTA}} V_{\text{EDTA}} = M_{\text{Ca}} V_{\text{Ca}} \implies V_{\text{EDTA}} = \frac{0.040 \times 25.0}{0.025} = 40.0\text{ mL}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A $10$-base-pair segment of double-stranded B-DNA contains $4$ adenine–thymine ($\text{A}-\text{T}$) pairs and $6$ guanine–cytosine ($\text{G}-\text{C}$) pairs. The total number of Watson–Crick hydrogen bonds holding the two strands together in this segment is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Each $\text{A}-\text{T}$ pair forms $2$ hydrogen bonds and each $\text{G}-\text{C}$ pair forms $3$ hydrogen bonds. Total hydrogen bonds $= 4(2) + 6(3) = 8 + 18 = \mathbf{26}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of open-chain stereoisomers possible for a **2-ketohexose** ($\text{HOCH}_2(\text{CHOH})_3\text{COCH}_2\text{OH}$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: An open-chain 2-ketohexose has $3$ chiral centers (C3, C4, C5), giving $2^3 = \mathbf{8}$ stereoisomers ($4$ D-isomers and $4$ L-isomers).

questions.questionTextEn: According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the bond order of the superoxide anion $\text{O}_2^-$ is _______. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn:
$\text{O}_2^-$ has $13$ valence electrons: $(\sigma_{2s})^2(\sigma^*_{2s})^2(\sigma_{2p_z})^2(\pi_{2p})^4(\pi^*_{2p})^3$.
Thus $N_b = 8$ and $N_a = 5$, giving $\text{BO} = \frac{8 - 5}{2} = 1.5$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Estimate the magnitude of the lattice energy $|U_0|$ (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) of $\text{MgCl}_2$ using the Kapustinskii equation:
$$|U_0| = \frac{1.214 \times 10^5\,\nu\,|z_+ z_-|}{r_+ + r_-}\left(1 - \frac{34.5}{r_+ + r_-}\right)$$
[Given: $r(\text{Mg}^{2+}) = 72\text{ pm}$; $r(\text{Cl}^-) = 181\text{ pm}$]
*(round off to the nearest integer)*

In a Cannizzaro reaction, $21.2\text{ g}$ of benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}$) is treated with concentrated aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ to yield $8.64\text{ g}$ of benzyl alcohol ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_8\text{O}$) along with sodium benzoate. The percentage yield of benzyl alcohol is _______ $\%$. *(round off to the nearest integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn:
Balanced Cannizzaro stoichiometry: $2\,\text{PhCHO} + \text{NaOH} \to \text{PhCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{PhCO}_2\text{Na}$.
- Moles of benzaldehyde $= 21.2 / 106 = 0.200\text{ mol}$.
- Theoretical moles of benzyl alcohol $= 0.200 / 2 = 0.100\text{ mol}$.
- Theoretical mass of benzyl alcohol $= 0.100 \times 108 = 10.80\text{ g}$.
- Percentage yield $= (8.64 / 10.80) \times 100\% = \mathbf{80}\%$.

questions.questionTextEn: Using the Debye–Hückel limiting law ($A = 0.509\text{ kg}^{1/2}\text{ mol}^{-1/2}$ at $298\text{ K}$), the mean ionic activity coefficient $\gamma_\pm$ of a $0.0040\text{ mol kg}^{-1}$ aqueous $\text{LaCl}_3$ solution is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
The neutral complex $[\text{Mn(CO)}_x(\text{NO})]$ obeys the $18$-electron rule and contains a linear nitrosyl ligand. The integer value of $x$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn:
Using the neutral-ligand method: $\text{Mn}$ ($7\text{ e}^-$) $+ \text{NO}_{\text{linear}}$ ($3\text{ e}^-$) $+ x\,\text{CO}$ ($2x\text{ e}^-$) $= 18$.
$10 + 2x = 18 \implies x = 4$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Among the following seven main-group species, the number of **planar** molecules/ions is _______.
$$\text{XeF}_4,\; [\text{ICl}_4]^-,\; \text{BrF}_3,\; [\text{XeF}_5]^-,\; \text{SF}_4,\; \text{XeO}_3,\; \text{IF}_5$$
questions.explanationEn:
Evaluating the molecular geometry of each species by VSEPR:
- $\text{XeF}_4$: square planar (planar — 1)
- $[\text{ICl}_4]^-$: square planar (planar — 2)
- $\text{BrF}_3$: T-shaped (all 4 atoms lie in one plane — 3)
- $[\text{XeF}_5]^-$: pentagonal planar (planar — 4)
- $\text{SF}_4$: seesaw (non-planar)
- $\text{XeO}_3$: trigonal pyramidal (non-planar)
- $\text{IF}_5$: square pyramidal (non-planar)
Thus, the total number of planar species is $4$.

questions.questionTextEn: A solution of a dye ($\varepsilon = 1204\text{ L mol}^{-1}\text{ cm}^{-1}$) placed in a $2.0\text{ cm}$ path-length cell transmits $25\%$ of the incident monochromatic light. The concentration of the dye is _______ $\text{mM}$ (millimolar). *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: With transmittance $T = 0.25$, the absorbance is $A = -\log_{10}(0.25) = 0.6021$. By Beer–Lambert law, $c = \frac{A}{\varepsilon l} = \frac{0.6021}{1204 \times 2.0} = 2.50 \times 10^{-4}\text{ M} = 0.25\text{ mM}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of chemically non-equivalent sets of protons in the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of *cis*-1,2-dimethylcyclopropane is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: In *cis*-1,2-dimethylcyclopropane ($C_s$ symmetry, mirror plane bisecting C1–C2 and passing through C3): (1) the two $-\text{CH}_3$ groups are equivalent ($6\text{H}$); (2) the two methine protons at C1 and C2 are equivalent ($2\text{H}$); (3) the C3 proton *syn* to the two methyl groups ($1\text{H}$) and (4) the C3 proton *anti* to the two methyl groups ($1\text{H}$) are **diastereotopic** and chemically non-equivalent. Hence there are $4$ signals in total.

questions.questionTextEn:
A reaction has an equilibrium constant $K_1 = 0.010$ at $300\text{ K}$ and a constant standard reaction enthalpy $\Delta_r H^\circ = +50.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Using the van 't Hoff equation, the equilibrium constant $K_2$ at $350\text{ K}$ is _______. *(round off to three decimal places)*
[Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: Using $\ln\left(\frac{K_2}{K_1}\right) = -\frac{\Delta_r H^\circ}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_2} - \frac{1}{T_1}\right) = -\frac{50{,}000}{8.314}\left(\frac{1}{350} - \frac{1}{300}\right) = +2.8638$. Therefore $K_2 = 0.010 \times e^{2.8638} \approx 0.176$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Exhaustive acetylation of **sucrose** ($\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$) with excess acetic anhydride in pyridine yields sucrose octaacetate. The molecular weight of sucrose octaacetate is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn:
Sucrose ($\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$, $\text{MW} = 342\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) has $8$ free $-\text{OH}$ groups. Replacing each $-\text{H}$ with an acetyl group ($-\text{COCH}_3$) adds $42\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ per $-\text{OH}$ group ($\text{C}_{28}\text{H}_{38}\text{O}_{19}$):
$\text{MW} = 342 + 8(42) = \mathbf{678}\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Calculate the EMF of the cell $\text{Zn}(s)\,|\,\text{Zn}^{2+}(0.10\text{ M})\,||\,\text{Ag}^+(0.010\text{ M})\,|\,\text{Ag}(s)$ at $298\text{ K}$ in $\text{V}$: _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
[Given: $E^\circ(\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}) = -0.76\text{ V}$, $E^\circ(\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}) = +0.80\text{ V}$, $\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.0591\text{ V}$]
